Spend enough time in Hell Harbor, and you pick up the paranoia encouraged by Arronax Endymion. Maybe you served under him on the Tyrannous, escaped his executioners, or had a friend who wasn't so lucky; whatever the reason, you have some of his wariness. Unless you're a willing target, you gain a +2 circumstance bonus to AC and saves against creatures you consider an ally and creatures who are undetected by you. If a creature you thought was an ally reveals itself as an enemy, you get the same bonus against them until the end of your next turn.

Additionally, the triggering ally's Leap distance on a successful check increases by 2 feet for a High Jump or 5 feet for a Long Jump, even if it would allow the ally to Leap further than their land Speed.

You've gotten the knack of using your oversized, webbed hands to rapidly shovel earth. You gain a burrow Speed of 15 feet.

You've learned how to make a quick descent with a sudden stop—directly on an enemy. You intentionally fall onto an enemy within 10 feet of you horizontally and can accurately target them from up to a height equal to 5 feet times your level. You take damage as normal; the enemy must attempt a

save against your class DC with the following results, instead of the usual rules for falling on a creature. If an ability reduces the amount of damage you take from falling, the enemy's damage is based on the damage you would have taken before that reduction. In addition, if you have a means of controlling your descent, such as holding onto a rope or sliding down an adjacent wall, you do not land
even if you take damage from the fall.

The enemy takes bludgeoning damage equal to one-quarter the falling damage you took.

You treat a well-planned assassination with the diligence that you would bring to any investigation. You can Pursue a Lead and open an investigation regarding a target you want to assassinate. This investigation doesn't count against the number of active investigations you can have at a time, but you can only have one assassination investigation.
Your Skill Stratagem bonus increases by 1 when investigating details about your assassination target.

You are a talented athlete trained to compete in swimming competitions, and would sometimes be asked to help your community settle disputes with others by participating in swimming races. When settling disputes with other aquatic or amphibious people, you can use Athletics instead of Diplomacy to Request.

When you use

, you can instead contemplate a person that you've gotten to observe within 30 feet for at least 1 minute. You deduce places they will habitually be in the next week and what time of day they'll be there. For each location, you deduce the likelihood that they will be two of the following: alone, unarmed, or unaware. You also gain a piece of advice for each location suggesting a course of action you or your allies could take that might make it more or less likely for them to be in the chosen states. The GM determines the locations the person will visit and when, as well as the likelihood they'll be alone, unarmed, or unaware.

Your eyes have adapted to the rigors of the sea. If you didn't already have darkvision, you gain darkvision. Additionally, you can see through natural phenomena that would obscure your vision underwater, such as cloudy waters, ink, smoke, and so forth, and don't need to succeed at a flat check to target creature within these phenomena. You developed techniques for discovering a target's weaknesses to poisons using your forensic knowledge. When you study a location that a creature spends a lot of time in, such as a bedroom or office, you learn medical conditions, reactions, or sensitivities that make them susceptible to poisons. Subsequently, whenever you craft an alchemical poison, you can tailor it to a creature you have studied in this way, giving that creature a –2 circumstance penalty to Fortitude saves against the poison and giving other creatures a +2 circumstance bonus to Fortitude saves against it.
alchemical sciences methodology
An animal has become your loyal ally, perhaps after you liberated it from another ship or found it on a remote island. You gain the

general feat. Your pet gains an additional pet ability, which you can choose from the standard pet abilities or the following familiar abilities: accompanist, damage avoidance, independent, partner in crime, speech, and valet.

In addition, you learn a common 1st- or 2nd-rank spell that targets your familiar, and can cast it once per day as a primal innate spell. You can instead learn phase familiar and can cast it once per hour as a primal innate spell; it's not a focus spell for you. When you cast the chosen spell, you target your pirate's pet instead of a familiar.
